about: Every headline claim this project makes, and what would fail if it were false. Not every sentence - the load-bearing ones, the ones a reader would quote. Defect §15 is why this file exists: two claims were graded PROVEN on evidence that did not support them, and nothing in the repository connected a claim to the test that was supposed to defend it.

grades.PROVEN: a test in this repository fails if this stops being true, AND a negative control shows the test can fail
grades.ADAPTER-PROVEN: the code is right; says nothing about any deployment or any database
grades.SKIPPED: not checked on a default run. Never reported as a pass
grades.DELEGATED: outside what the engine can see. The caller answers it
grades.NOT-CLAIMED: the arithmetic does not support it and no document asserts it

rules.everyClaimNeedsATest: A claim with no `test` is a claim nobody is defending. PROVEN and ADAPTER-PROVEN require one.
rules.provenNeedsANegativeControl: A PROVEN claim needs something deliberately broken that the test rejects - a mutant, a fake, or a mutation entry. Otherwise it is §15: a test that passes and could not fail.
rules.numbersMustBeGenerated: A numeric claim must name the script that produces it. `pnpm audit:claims` re-runs that script and compares. Four separate passes of this project shipped a stale hand-typed number.
rules.notClaimedNeedsNoTest: NOT-CLAIMED and DELEGATED claims are about what is NOT asserted. The prose guard defends those, not a unit test.

claims.claim: The policy engine is pure: no imports, no clock, no randomness, nothing async.
claims.negativeControl: mutation entry `core-purity`: adding a node:fs import to policy.ts must fail the contract test
claims.note: The import half of this check was VACUOUS from the day it was written until v1.0 - the stripper blanked string literals before the scan, so it matched nothing. See DEFECTS_FOUND.md §16.

claims.claim: The 16 v0 holdout cases have not changed, byte for byte.
claims.negativeControl: a formatter rewrote three files once and the manifest caught it - defect §5

claims.claim: 34 imported cases rebuild byte-identically from committed upstream source rows.
claims.negativeControl: editing one imported string makes the rebuild diverge and the check exits 1

claims.claim: A receipt admits one value, into one slot, once - and a label-only receipt matches nothing where the label repeats.
claims.negativeControl: mutant M9 argname_only_binding, bitten by corpus slot-t-001 and nothing else

claims.claim: When the guard loses a receipt race it re-decides rather than returning the stale verdict.
claims.negativeControl: a store that reports unspent on read and already-taken on write
claims.note: Graded PROVEN in v0.9 on a test that could not fail. Deleting the branch left 74/74 passing. See DEFECTS_FOUND.md §15.

claims.claim: Every capability table in this repository has zero structural contradictions.
claims.negativeControl: the tests construct contradictory manifests and assert each code fires

claims.claim: Every mutant is bitten somewhere and none is bitten everywhere; the reference is bitten by nothing.
claims.negativeControl: the bite matrix exits 1 if any mutant is bitten by nothing or by everything

claims.claim: 69 of 69 silent attacks are contained; the classifier catches 0.
claims.negativeControl: the labelling convention test asserts no silent-labelled attack is flagged by classify()

claims.claim: The policy engine special-cases no business domain: no refund, ticket, deploy, kubernetes, invoice, solana or USDC anywhere in its code.
claims.negativeControl: the test scans policy.ts source; adding the word fails it
claims.note: Stated precisely because the first version of this entry said "no wallet" - which is FALSE: `wallet` appears four times in policy.ts, because `wallet_sign` is a capability name, and it was never in the scanned word list. The claim is about the engine not branching on a DOMAIN, not about the absence of a substring. `wallet_sign` names a capability class - irreversible, full egress, nothing lifts it - and its BEHAVIOUR is domain-independent; only its name is not. Caught by an adversarial audit of this registry. See DEFECTS_FOUND.md §17.

claims.claim: No document asserts a freeze proof, calls Postgres proven without its condition, implies a validated manifest is honest, claims the workflows prove judgement, or asserts optimality.
claims.negativeControl: an injected false claim is demonstrably caught - see audit:docs

claims.claim: Concurrent reserve, cross-process replay refusal, restart durability, crash handling and bounded stale reclaim hold against a real Postgres.
claims.negativeControl: a read-then-write adapter in the same script must double-claim
claims.note: PROVEN only on a run with DATABASE_URL. Without it the whole block reports SKIPPED / NOT PROVEN.

claims.claim: The reserve/decide/consume-or-release protocol never spends a receipt behind a refusal.
claims.negativeControl: a read-then-write async adapter fails exactly one conformance scenario

claims.claim: The sync cross-host claim is earned by passing five interleavings, not asserted.
claims.negativeControl: nonAtomicStore fails exactly the concurrent double-spend scenario

claims.claim: Without DATABASE_URL the real-database proof reports SKIPPED / NOT PROVEN and exits 0.
Whether your hosts point at one database is a question the caller answers.
Whether a capability declaration is honest cannot be established from the declaration.
No policy here is proven optimal. Five profiles, two undominated.
That the holdout predates the engine is UNAVAILABLE, not pending.
A tool declared weaker than it is lets 9 of 17 direct-harm and 17 of 17 data-stealing imported attacks through.
The taint wrapper is cooperative, not enforced. There is no membrane in JavaScript.
